title: SIEM-export-design-and-customer-questionnaire-notes
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a working note intended to align engineering, product, and customer-facing teams on a concise SIEM export design that satisfies common customer questionnaires and evidence requests. Focus areas: RBAC v2 implications, audit log canonical schema, SIEM export formats (JSON/CEF), and automated evidence bundles for customer questionnaires.

Audience:
- Prospective enterprise buyers asking for SIEM export and log evidence
- Solutions engineers preparing customer responses
- Infra/serving teams implementing log sinks and exporters

High-level goals:
1) Define a minimal canonical audit-log schema that covers RBAC v2 events, policy changes, auth events, and sensitive data access markers.
2) Produce export adapters for JSON and CEF to meet typical SIEM ingestion pipelines.
3) Draft canned questionnaire answers and a checklist for evidence automation (one-pagers + sample logs).
4) Identify operational controls to protect PII in exported logs and retention/sampling policies.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments must be supported; Private can restrict external syslog sinks.
- Customers commonly require both near-real-time forwarding and batched evidence exports for audits.
- RBAC v2 introduces role-versioning and grant provenance fields that must be captured.

Canonical audit-log schema (minimal fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id (uuid)
- service (string) e.g., "redwood-api" or "rbac-service"
- event_type (string) e.g., "auth.login", "rbac.role.update", "model.invoke"
- actor_id (string) stable internal user id or system principal id
- actor_type (string) e.g., "human", "service", "api-key"
- actor_principal (string) email or service name when allowed by policy
- target_resource (string) resource path or id, e.g., "projects/prod/model-abc/route-1"
- action (string) e.g., "grant", "revoke", "create", "call"
- outcome (string) "success" | "failure" | "throttled"
- reason (string, optional) free-text lower-cardinality reason or error code
- rbac_version (string) e.g., "v2"
- rbac_change (string, optional) short summary for role changes e.g., "added-perm:read_logs"
- grant_provenance (string, optional) e.g., "admin-console", "api-key-rotation-job"
- request_id (string) cross-service correlation id
- request_latency_ms (number as string)
- ip_address (string, optional, masked by policy)
- host (string) the originating host/instance id
- raw_payload (string, optional) serialized request body (redacted by default)
- redaction_state (string) e.g., "redacted-pii", "full"

Notes on RBAC v2 specifics:
- Record role-version ids rather than textual role names: role_id and role_version to enable deterministic replay during audits.
- Capture grant_provenance so customer auditors can trace whether grants were created by console, automation, or API.
- For bulk role changes include a granular diff summary in rbac_change and link to an artifact id (PR or automation job id).

SIEM export adapters (requirements):
- JSONL (newline-delimited JSON) file sink for batched export and forensic artifact packaging.
  - Include a manifest.json with schema version, timeframe, and sample count.
- CEF compatibility layer: map canonical fields into CEF fields and include event_id as cs1 (custom1) for traceability.
- Syslog/HTTPS forwarder for near-real-time: support TLS, mutual auth for private nets, and HEC-like tokens for Splunk.
- Compression: support gzip level 3 by default for batch uploads.

Example JSONL event (canonical):
{"timestamp":"2024-11-18T15:22:03Z","event_id":"e7b7c2f4-8a0a-4c2f-bc3f-1d4f0a9a8b7c","service":"rbac-service","event_type":"rbac.role.update","actor_id":"user-1243","actor_type":"human","actor_principal":"alice@example.com","target_resource":"org/1234/role/engineering-readonly","action":"update","outcome":"success","rbac_version":"v2","rbac_change":"added-perm:read_logs;removed-perm:exec_snapshots","grant_provenance":"admin-console","request_id":"r-9a8b7c6d","redaction_state":"redacted-pii","host":"rbac-03.prod"}

CEF mapping guidance (short):
- CEF header: CEF:0|Redwood|InferencePlatform|1.0|<event_type>|<short_desc>|<severity>|
- Map event_id -> cs1Label=event_id, cs1 -> event_id
- Map actor_principal -> shost (if permitted) or cs2 masked
- Map rbac_change -> msg or cs3
- Use extension fields for request_id, host, service.

PII & redaction policy (operational):
- Default export strips emails and IPs (replace local-part with *** if customer allows more context in dedicated/private).
- Provide opt-in toggles for "full-identity" export under enterprise contract with explicit data processing addendum and KMS-based keying for transport.
- Evidence exports for audits: produce a redaction manifest that explains what was redacted and why.

Automated evidence bundle (proposal):
- For customer questionnaires marked high-risk, produce a zipped bundle containing:
  - manifest.json (schema, time window, retention policy)
  - sample_jsonl.log (up to X events, configurable by customer)
  - sample_cef.log (same events translated)
  - mapping_document.txt (this doc excerpt explaining fields)
  - audit_trace_links.txt (Jira ids and internal run ids used to generate samples)
- Bundle generation is initiated by Solutions Engineering or automatically triggered by a "evidence-request" label in the security ticketing queue.

Suggested canned responses for customer questionnaires (short snippets, editable):
Q: Do you export audit logs to customer SIEM?
A: Yes — Redwood supports push-based and pull-based export of audit logs. Exports can be delivered in JSONL or CEF formats over TLS, and customers can request batched bundles for audits. Exports redact PII by default; explicit unredacted export options are available under enterprise agreements.

Q: Do logs include RBAC change history?
A: Yes — all RBAC v2 changes are logged with role_id and role_version, a compact diff in rbac_change, and grant_provenance metadata to support forensic review.

Q: Can exports be sent to our on-prem SIEM?
A: Yes — for Dedicated and Private deployments we support syslog over TLS and mutual-auth HTTPS endpoints. For Hosted, we can configure a secure, inbound-only endpoint or provide batched S3-style artifacts if direct push is not possible.

Operational checklist for implementation (MVP):
- [ ] Finalize canonical schema v1.0 (this doc) and register in internal schema registry (SEC-SCHEMA-001)
- [ ] Implement JSONL batch exporter and manifest generator (infra ticket JIRA-OPS-2101)
- [ ] Implement CEF mapping module and validation tests
- [ ] Add redaction engine hooks for emails and IPs with policy flags
- [ ] Wire export auth: mTLS and HMAC token support
- [ ] Create solutions engineering playbook and canned questionnaire library
- [ ] End-to-end runbook for evidence bundle generation and approval flow

Open questions / items needing product/security sign-off:
- What is the default retention window for exported artifacts in Hosted (30/90/365 days)? Suggestions: 90 days for standard, 365 for enterprise.
- How granular should the redaction manifest be to satisfy auditors without leaking content? Need legal input.
- Should we include sampled model input snippets in audit logs for debugging (privacy risk)? If yes, we need explicit consent and strong redaction.

References & tickets:
- SEC-4321 (confluence design page)
- JIRA-OPS-2101 (exporter implementation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/789 (initial exporter code)

Next steps (owner: Evelyn Chen):
1) Review with Product Security and Legal (target: 2024-11-25)
2) Spin ticket for JSONL exporter and assign to infra (target: 2024-12-05)
3) Draft solutions-engineering one-pager with two canned evidence bundles (target: 2024-12-12)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a "trace id" index for quick lookups across SIEM and internal traces — could help during customer incident triage.
- For private deployments, offer a small agent that pushes encrypted batches to customer S3 with manifest and PGP-signed metadata.

End of notes. This document is intentionally terse and operational — expand into a full spec once we lock answers to the open questions above.
